ASSESS: Strongest feature: Loeb directly challenges an uncomplicated convergence narrative with concrete countervailing developments, pointing to renewed authoritarianism and racism as evidence that apparent moral gains can be unstable or reversible. Principal limitation: Short-term or regional reversals do not negate long-run, noisy, or nonmonotonic progress, and the move supplies no historical baseline capable of weighing setbacks against broader institutional change. Live burden: He needed to show that reversals are extensive enough to weaken Huemer’s truth-tracking interpretation rather than merely illustrating that progress, if real, is vulnerable and incomplete.
REVIEWS: accepted: Loeb relies on recent or regional authoritarian and racist reversals to reduce confidence in broad moral progress without weighing their scale against the much longer historical period and wider institutional changes at issue. || accepted: Loeb gives recent or regional authoritarian and racist reversals substantial weight against moral progress without a historical baseline that measures them against broader, long-run institutional change. The assessment specifically identifies this mismatch between local setbacks and the scale of the progress claim.

IDX 24 | pro-15 | fallacy | Begging the question
DEF: Assuming, directly or indirectly, the very point that needs to be established, so the conclusion is smuggled into the premises.
EXCERPT: well okay but before 1800 basically every society was was a dictatorship and now you know about half the world is democratic so that's pretty big progress and you know we don't we don't know what's going to happen in the future nobody knows but and um you know not but I claim that yeah well the reason why we made this progress is uh democracy is better than dictatorship and then like people figure that out
ASSESS: Strongest feature: Huemer answers recent reversals by widening the historical frame and presenting democratization as a concrete, large-scale directional change that plausibly counts as moral and political progress. Principal limitation: The numerical historical claims are broad estimates, and the inference from democratization to recognition of objective moral superiority does not exclude economic, military, institutional, technological, or desire-based explanations. Live burden: He needed evidence connecting the transition specifically to moral discovery and a comparative account showing why Loeb’s suffering-reduction and control-satisfaction mechanisms do not predict the same pattern.
REVIEWS: rejected: Calling democratization progress and attributing it to recognition of democracy's superiority leaves major rival causes untested, but the move does not clearly smuggle stance-independent realism itself into a premise. The assessed defect is rival-explanation failure. || rejected: Calling democratization progress and democracy better risks assuming evaluative conclusions relevant to realism, but the argument's stated causal claim is that people recognized this superiority. The assessment's defect is failure to compare rival causal explanations, not a demonstrated circular premise.
URL: https://logfall.com/fallacies/begging-the-question/

IDX 25 | pro-16 | bias | Confirmation bias
DEF: Seeking, interpreting, or remembering evidence in ways that favor an existing view while discounting contrary information.
EXCERPT: comment um if uh if convergence on the non-moral facts leads to convergence on the moral facts then I think that's evidence of moral realism like you know that suggests that oh the reason why we were disagreeing in the first place was that we didn't know the non-moral facts so you know once we know them then we're going to agree because you know self-evident moral truths or
ASSESS: Strongest feature: Huemer makes the evidential bridge explicit: if convergence on non-moral facts predictably produces convergence in moral judgment, earlier disagreement may reflect factual ignorance rather than absence of shared moral truth. Principal limitation: The move provides no concrete convergence cases or rival-prediction analysis, and shared desires, aversions, social aims, or reasoning procedures could also generate fact-sensitive agreement under anti-realism. Live burden: He needed to show that the observed conditional pattern is more expected given common self-evident moral truths than given Loeb’s attitude- and function-based alternatives.
REVIEWS: rejected: Huemer interprets fact-sensitive convergence as realist evidence without comparing anti-realist predictions, but the source does not show selective evidence processing motivated by an existing belief. The exact assessed weakness is missing comparative analysis. || rejected: Huemer interprets fact-sensitive convergence as evidence congenial to realism without comparing anti-realist predictions, but no selective search, interpretation pattern, memory distortion, or discounting of contrary information is established. The assessment supports weak comparative warrant, not inferred bias.
URL: https://cogbias.site/biases/confirmation-bias/

pro-04 | fallacy | Begging the question
DEF Assuming, directly or indirectly, the very point that needs to be established, so the conclusion is smuggled into the premises.
EX I mean so my claim is like all of the all the beliefs that are reasonable candidates for being considered Justified are based upon the way things seem to you
ASSESS Strongest feature: Huemer clearly states the comprehensive epistemological premise his moral realism requires, connecting every reasonable candidate for justified belief with how matters seem to the believer. Principal limitation: The universal formulation receives no supporting cases or clarifying distinctions, leaving “based upon” and “seems” insufficiently specified across perception, memory, testimony, inference, and theoretically mediated belief. Live burden: Because objective moral appearances support realism only if this foundational entitlement is defensible, he must explain how seemings generate prima facie justification, how defeaters constrain them, and why the account does not simply presuppose their authority.
REV rejected: The universal claim that justified beliefs rest on seemings is asserted without support and leaves key terms unclear, but this move does not yet explicitly derive the authority of seemings by assuming that same authority. Underdevelopment alone is insufficient. || rejected: The assessment warns that Huemer must explain why his account does not presuppose the authority of seemings, making circularity a serious concern. This isolated move, however, merely states the foundational thesis without using that thesis as its own supporting premise, so underargument is insufficient.
URL https://logfall.com/fallacies/begging-the-question/

pro-05 | fallacy | Begging the question
DEF Assuming, directly or indirectly, the very point that needs to be established, so the conclusion is smuggled into the premises.
EX can't check on perception without using perception you can't check on reason without using reason you can't check on the velocity of memory without using memory also you can't check on intuitions without using intuitions so you can check them using other intuitions that is you can have intuitions that fit together and support each other right and that increases their justification
ASSESS Strongest feature: Huemer gives the circularity objection a disciplined comparative structure, noting that perception, reason, memory, and intuition inevitably participate in their own assessment while mutually supporting intuitions can strengthen coherence. Principal limitation: Unavoidable self-use does not establish comparable reliability, corrective mechanisms, subject matter, or resistance to cultural influence, and internally coherent intuitions may still share one systematically misleading origin. Live burden: He must show that moral intuition resembles established faculties in truth-conducive characteristics rather than merely circular validation, while explaining when coherence genuinely increases justification instead of reorganizing antecedent commitments.
REV rejected: Mutually supporting intuitions create a serious circularity concern, but Huemer is expressly offering coherence and parity with other faculties rather than covertly inserting the final realist conclusion into a premise. The assessment identifies inadequate reliability comparison instead.
URL https://logfall.com/fallacies/begging-the-question/

con-10 | fallacy | Begging the question
DEF Assuming, directly or indirectly, the very point that needs to be established, so the conclusion is smuggled into the premises.
EX Well we'd need to say more maybe maybe my things he already has I'm not convinced about why we should take seemings as evidence for beings right as evidence for the way things are we don't want to presume that the presumption is Justified right that would be circular
ASSESS Strongest feature: Loeb targets the exact epistemic bridge on which Huemer’s realism depends, insisting that entitlement to move from how matters seem to how they are cannot be secured merely by presuming that entitlement. Principal limitation: Calling the view circular does not answer the possibility that seemings provide basic, non-inferential prima facie warrant, and the passage offers no counterexample or independent standard demonstrating that such warrant fails. Live burden: Loeb needed to distinguish objectionable premise-assumption from foundational justification and explain why moral seemings specifically require additional support, particularly after Huemer argued that any proposed criterion must itself seem correct.
REV rejected: Loeb accuses a presumption favoring seemings of circularity, but his own move does not assume the anti-realist conclusion it must establish. Its defect is failure to answer basic non-inferential warrant, not question-begging as defined. || rejected: Loeb alleges that presuming the evidential authority of seemings would be circular, but his own move does not assume the conclusion that seemings lack prima facie warrant. The assessment instead finds that he fails to answer a non-inferential foundational account, an omission rather than question-begging.
URL https://logfall.com/fallacies/begging-the-question/

con-11 | fallacy | Argument from ignorance
DEF Treating a claim as true because it has not been disproved, or false because it has not been proved, rather than supplying positive evidence.
EX um I think we should take seeming seriously when the best explanation for things seeming in certain way is that they are that way and that's very hard to evaluate for sure but I think that we should only do so in those circumstances and I don't think um God and morality fit into that category so far yeah before turning it
ASSESS Strongest feature: Loeb advances a positive alternative to blanket skepticism, proposing that a seeming warrants belief when the represented reality provides the best explanation for why the appearance occurs. Principal limitation: He neither defends this explanationist condition as necessary nor compares actual explanations of moral experience, so the verdict that morality has not met the test remains largely asserted. Live burden: He needed criteria for explanatory superiority and evidence showing cultural, emotional, or practical accounts outperform truth-tracking realism, while answering Huemer’s regress-style objection that accepting explanationism ultimately depends on something seeming correct.
REV rejected: Loeb withholds trust because moral truth has not been shown to provide the best explanation of moral seemings; he does not infer that moral realism is false merely because it remains unproved. The assessment instead faults his unsupported explanatory criterion and verdict. || rejected: Saying moral seemings have not yet satisfied an explanationist condition approaches a proof-deficit inference, but Loeb's conclusion is only that trust is not yet warranted, not that realism is false. The assessment records an asserted and undefended test, not the exact catalog fallacy.
URL https://logfall.com/fallacies/argument-from-ignorance/
